title: Two-path recovery: scheduled pg_dump artefact PLUS vendor point-in-time recovery, both required, cadence elicited
context: A shipped Postgres project has to survive two failure classes: a corrupted or lost cluster (a managed-Postgres outage, a self-managed disk failure, a bad DBA operation) and a data-integrity incident an operator wants to unwind by minutes or hours (a bug that deleted rows, a bad migration a rollback file cannot invert). pg_dump gives a portable off-cluster artefact; vendor PITR (a managed cluster's window, a self-managed cluster's WAL-archive posture) gives fine-grained restore points. Neither alone covers both failure classes.
decision: The shipped recovery model requires both paths: (a) a scheduled pg_dump runner (TAC-2804) writes an artefact to the elicited destination on an elicited cadence, and (b) the deploy target's own point-in-time recovery is enabled with an elicited PITR window (a managed cluster's retention setting; a self-managed cluster's WAL-archive retention). Neither path is optional; a project that answers off to either fails the ADR's apply-time check. A recovery drill (US-27110) periodically primes a fresh Postgres from the artefact and compares row-count and checksum against the source; the drill's cadence is elicited.
consequences: The project survives both failure classes: a portable off-cluster artefact for cluster loss and a fine-grained PITR window for data-integrity incidents. Storage cost is two-path (artefact bytes off-cluster plus WAL retention on-cluster); the operator sizes both per RTO/RPO. The drill catches artefact-shape drift (a pg_dump on a new engine version producing a different plain-format shape) before an incident forces a live restore. Standards trace clause: generic enterprise practice.

alternativesConsidered.name: pg_dump only
alternativesConsidered.summary: Ship pg_dump as the sole recovery path; skip vendor PITR.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: A pg_dump artefact taken hourly can lose up to 59 minutes of writes; an operator restoring after a bad migration loses everything committed between the last dump and the incident. PITR bounds that loss to the WAL-shipping cadence.

alternativesConsidered.name: PITR only
alternativesConsidered.summary: Rely on the deploy target's own PITR window; skip the pg_dump runner.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: PITR does not survive cluster loss: if the managed cluster is gone, the retention window is gone with it. A portable off-cluster artefact is what carries across cluster loss.
